summary: Plan check, round 3 (22:35 UTC 25 Sep). The 00:01 UTC submission of K2 (exp58 v1) and the twin (exp58n v1) is safe to run as planned. Both Kaggle kernels are COMPLETE. The twin's pulled source is identical to the local build (12/12 code cells). R7 hygiene flags are off (VALIDATOR_ENABLE 0, DIVINS_DUMP 0, no lab lines). The local clock is within 2 s of Kaggle and the PC never sleeps. A ledger simulation with the proposed messages auto-detects K2 (family safetail) and the twin (safetail_noins), so no --k2 flag and no poller restart are needed. The main gaps are in the rules, not the artefacts. (1) No rule says which scored file K2 is compared with under R3 (#35 0.954 or #34 0.953). K2's probe.json even says 'compare with exp56'. (2) The K1 fallback (v4 item 6) covers only a K2 ERROR. It does not cover K2 <= 0.952 (lowrefine fails R3; the twin contains lowrefine too) or twin - K2 >= +0.002 (R2 reopens; F2 is then undefined). Both cases must be written into CONTEXT before about 06:30 UTC, when the scores can appear. Other items: the task's plan still lists K3/K3b builds, which the pre-registered T9 read closed. poll.log keeps only the 5 newest submissions. The last RESUME POINT and the §10 checklist are stale and contradict PRE-REGISTRATION v3. The A5 forecast F can now be computed (7.87 h < 7.9 h). The 00:05 quota check has almost no remaining purpose.

findings.what: The R3 reference for K2 is undefined. K2 = #35 + C01 (safetail, inert unless a deadline fires; K1 sha == exp57b dummy) + C05 (lowrefine). R3 says 'public >= previous stack - 0.001', but CONTEXT never names the previous stack. If it is #35 (0.954), K2 = 0.952 fails R3. If it is #34 (0.953), K2 = 0.952 passes. The K2 artefact itself says something else: experiments/exp58_x138_safe_lowref/probe.json 'rule' = 'compare with exp56 ... above exp56 adopt, ties recorded' (builder boilerplate). Under that wording K2 = 0.953 would be only a 'tie', not an adoption. Choosing the reference after K2 scores (~06:30-08:00 UTC) would be choosing the rule by the result.

findings.action: Before 06:00 UTC, write into CONTEXT (timestamped, before any K2 score): 'R3 reference for K2 = #35 (0.954), the scored file with the same insertion config. A K2 delta is attributed to lowrefine only (C01 is inert unless a deadline fires; FD/FF/K1 dummies). If L(K2) > 8.0 h, a K2 drop may come from the insertion gate firing on late clips, not from lowrefine. It is then read as a timing confound, as in branch C, and not as lowrefine harm.' Add a second check: twin - #34 <= -0.002 also closes lowrefine. The twin = #34 + C01 + C05 isolates lowrefine without the insertion. The probe.json boilerplate is not a rule; say so in the same entry.

findings.what: The K2/twin read table has holes that land on bad finals. (a) K2 <= 0.952: R3 closes lowrefine. The §f fallback is then 'previous K' (none) -> K1 (unscored; approved only for branches C/D or a K2 ERROR under v4 item 6 [OK]) -> #35 (not admissible, L35 in (6.72, 7.73] h is unproven) -> #34, a byte-copy of x138 at the END of the 241-team tie block. The twin also contains lowrefine, yet f2 would still make it F2 if it scores >= 0.953. That conflicts with R3's 'removed and never tried again'. (b) twin - K2 >= +0.002: R2 reopens, the insertion leaves the F1 stack and the twin becomes F1. F2 is then undefined, because f2 names exp52 only when the twin is unscored or failed, or in branch D. (c) K2 ERROR plus twin ERROR: covered only by item 6 plus exp52.

findings.what: The submit checklist is verified; four details matter. (1) The twin's message must have 'exp58n' as its FIRST exp token. A message like 'probe 38: K2 twin (exp58 minus insertion) = exp58n' would make the ledger pick the twin as K2 (token exp58) with the wrong family and a false insertion-gate column. (2) Submit both with -v 1. exp58 v1 ran at 16:20:17Z and exp58n v1 at 20:35:41Z; neither has been re-pushed since its dummy. (3) Submit at >= 00:01:00 UTC: 25 Sep is full (5 submissions), and the local clock is within 2 s of Kaggle. (4) A ledger simulation with the proposed messages gives K2 = safetail (9.5 h, insertion-gate column) and twin = safetail_noins. The round-2 advice to add --k2/--family to the poller (which needs a restart) is therefore unnecessary.

findings.what: poll.log records only the 5 newest submissions. lb_poll.py writes out.strip().splitlines()[:12], and the Kaggle CLI output separates rows with blank lines, so 12 lines = header + 5 rows. After 00:01 the window holds twin, K2, P36, #35 and #34. A pending K build drops out of the window after 4 newer submissions. After that, runtime_ledger never sees its COMPLETE. hi_h stays None and R5(a) and the insertion-gate proof become UNPROVEN forever. This is harmless tonight, but it bites on a busy day (26-28 Sep, 5 slots) while an earlier K build is still pending.

findings.what: The A5 forecast F (round-2 PC2-12, never computed) can now be computed from the dummies with the v4 item-5 formula. Repair delta K2 vs exp57b dummy = (509.2 - 491.4)/4 = 4.45 s/clip, and 97 * 4.45 * 1.15 = 496 s = 0.14 h. So F = L35_upper 7.73 + 0.14 = 7.87 h, just below the 7.9 h trigger. lowrefine costs about nothing in the GPU phase: Prediction took 9.30 min for K2 vs 9.18 for exp57b, but 9.40 for the twin (same lowrefine) and 9.22 for K1, so it is noise. Start-up before the first repair varies 818-1179 s between identical-code kernels. Consequence: the 7.9 h trigger sits inside the noise, and L(K2) > 8.0 h can come from queueing alone. The twin, submitted at the same moment with the same GPU phase but ~65 s/clip less repair, is a paired control for that.
